m3-damped-resonance.title: Two solutions from Lecture 8: y = e⁻ˣ·cos 2x — complex roots −1 ± 2i give a damped oscillation (quick classification table, slide 18) — and the resonant particular solution y = −(x/2)·cos x of y″ + y = sin x, whose amplitude grows like x/2 (slide 31)

m3-fourier-square.title: Square wave (−1 on [−π, 0), 1 on [0, π)) and the partial sums SN(x) = (4/π) Σ sin((2k−1)x)/(2k−1): more harmonics give a better approximation; at the jumps the sums pass through 0, the average of the one-sided limits (Lecture 5, slides 13, 18 and 34)

m3-xn-nonuniform.title: fₙ(x) = xⁿ on [0, 1]: the curves tend to 0 for every x < 1, but near x = 1 the error sup|xⁿ − f(x)| stays equal to 1, so the convergence is not uniform (Lecture 1, slides 5 and 14)
